lead: Water heater installation in Oakley, CA, planned ahead: the right size, the right venting, strapping and a clean hookup.
Pick your day, and we handle the details before the old unit is out.
intro: Water heater installation is the planned setting of a new tank, tankless or heat pump unit, including sizing, fuel connections, venting, drain and earthquake strapping. In Oakley, CA, the work is usually done in a garage, closet or side yard in a home built since the 1980s, when most of the city's housing arrived.

This page is for scheduled jobs, so you have time to compare fuel types and ask the City about permits. If your current tank is already flooding, our [[water-heater-replacement|replacement page]] covers the emergency route.

sections.h2: Sizing the unit to your household
paras: Size comes from how many people shower in the same hour, how many bathrooms you have and whether a soaking tub or a long laundry run is part of daily life. A tank that is too small runs out of hot water, and one that is too big burns fuel keeping extra water warm.

We look at first-hour capacity for tanks and flow rate for tankless units, then match it to the space you actually have. Bring up any plan to add a bathroom, an in-law unit or a pool house, because that changes the answer.

sections.h2: Rules that shape an Oakley install
paras: Fuel choice is partly a rules question. The Air District's zero-NOx date for residential gas water heaters moved from January 2027 to January 2028 under amendments adopted on November 4, 2026, and that date matters only for a unit being newly installed, never for one already in service.
Check baaqmd.gov for the exemptions that came with the later date before you order a gas unit.

Any new or replacement tank must be braced or strapped under Health and Safety Code 19211, using a strapping kit for standard units of 120 gallons or less. Before booking an install, ask the City of Oakley Building Division at 925-625-7005 if it needs a permit, and plan around the permit counter at 3231 Main Street being open Monday through Thursday.

sections.h2: What moves the price of a planned install
paras: Because there is no emergency, you can compare options calmly. These are the pieces that decide the total.

factors.d: The unit itself leads the bill, and tankless and heat pump models run higher than basic tanks.
Relocating a unit means new supply, drain and venting or electrical runs.
Gas to electric or the reverse needs a new circuit or gas line.
Seismic strapping, an expansion tank, a drain pan and a proper relief discharge line are standard parts of a clean install.
If the City requires a permit, plan for the time to obtain it. Ask the Building Division what applies.

sections.insurance: A planned upgrade is normally an owner expense. Some insurers ask for proof of water-damage prevention features, so ask yours whether a pan, leak sensor or auto-shutoff earns anything.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 and we will walk through the options and give a clear price before work starts.

paras: A little preparation shortens the visit and avoids surprises.

items.d: Move stored items in the garage or closet so the old unit and new unit can pass without bumping into things.
Photograph the rating plate showing fuel, capacity and model. We can plan parts from it.
Find the main water shutoff and, for gas, the gas shutoff. If you cannot locate either, tell us.
Water to the whole house is off for part of the visit, so plan showers and laundry around it.
If you might add a bathroom or solar, say so before we choose the unit.

sections.h2: Strapping, expansion and the small parts that matter
paras: The installer's craft shows in the pieces nobody sees afterward. A closed plumbing system with a backflow device on the supply can trap pressure when the water heats, and an expansion tank gives it somewhere to go.

A relief valve with a full-size discharge line, a drain pan with a path to a safe spot and flexible connectors with isolation valves all make later service easier. If your home needs [[plumbing-installation|other fixture or line work]] at the same time, schedule it together so walls are opened once. We serve nearby [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]] with the same approach.

faqs.q: How long does a water heater installation take?
a: A standard swap of the same type is often a half-day job. Changing fuel type, adding a vent or running a new circuit extends it, and we tell you before booking.

faqs.q: What size water heater do I need?
a: It depends on the number of people, bathrooms and appliances using hot water in the same hour. We size from first-hour capacity or flow rate and check that it fits your space.

faqs.q: Can I convert from gas to a heat pump water heater?
a: Often, if there is room, clearance, a condensate path and a 240-volt circuit. Ask your electric provider about incentives.

faqs.q: Does the Air District rule stop me from installing a gas heater?
a: For new residential gas units the zero-NOx standard now starts in January 2028. The Air District website carries the rule text.
Yes. Health and Safety Code 19211 requires new and replacement water heaters to be braced, anchored or strapped, and we include it.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to install a water heater in Oakley?
a: The City does not list water heater work specifically, so a quick call to the Building Division settles it. Permits can go to the owner, an agent or a CSLB-licensed contractor.

faqs.q: Do you install tankless units too?
a: Yes, after checking gas line size, venting and power. Our tankless page covers service and descaling.
